summary: Analysis only, based on reading the source. Nothing was run or rendered. I propose three changes. (1) Fix the dash patterns so they mean something: right now unreviewed and superseded links look identical, and the "marching" requirement arcs shown on focus look like drafts. (2) Bundle arcs by framework pair and wash weak bundles toward the background to cut the tangle. (3) Show focus with color only, no transparency: dim pillar instance colors and draw faint context arcs from the existing geometry. All three keep positions, the camera, the 2D list and the mapping data unchanged, and they allow on-demand rendering with no animation loop.
design:
1. DASH PATTERNS THAT MATCH THE LEGEND. Problems: LINK_DASH gives unreviewed and superseded the same pattern. The focused requirement arcs march with a 1.6/0.5 dash, which reads as "draft". And because computeLineDistances adds distance across the whole batch, each arc starts its pattern at a random point. Fix: final = solid; draft = long dash (1.2 on, 0.6 off); unreviewed = dense dots (0.45 on, 0.55 off); superseded = sparse dots (0.45 on, 1.6 off) plus extra wash. Requirement mappings are always solid, and nothing moves. At home distance (about 120 units, fov 45, 800px tall) one world unit is about 8px, so 0.45 units is about 3.6px: a dot that stays visible next to 1–3px lines.

2. BUNDLE BY FRAMEWORK PAIR. Endpoints stay where they are. Arcs between the same two frameworks share a trunk, using a cubic Bezier instead of the quadratic: c1 = lerp(a, hubA, β), c2 = lerp(z, hubB, β). hubX is the middle of that framework's sector, pulled inward to the same radius factor as today's control point (0.18 for the outer ring, 0.7 for threat arcs). It is raised to Y = the pair's average control height. β ≈ 0.55. Wash depends on how many mappings a bundle carries: wash = 0.25 + 0.45·(1 − √count/√maxCount). Strong mappings stay in their framework colors and weak ones fade toward the background. Resting arcs are opaque, so set depthWrite true on them. That gives real 3D overlap instead of whichever batch happened to draw last. Draw batches thin-to-thick.

3. FOCUS WITHOUT TRANSPARENCY. Pillars become one InstancedMesh per shape (outer hexagon, inner triangle) with an opaque material. To dim a pillar, lerp its instance color 70% toward TOKENS.neutral instead of setting opacity 0.32. This avoids transparency sorting problems and keeps one draw call. Arcs: instead of hiding resting arcs on focus, draw the same resting geometry a second time with a shared "ghost" LineMaterial (linewidth 1, opacity ≈ 0.14, transparent). On the flat neutral background this works like a lerp toward the canvas, so the context stays visible and nothing is rebuilt. The focused arcs draw on top, 1.35× wider, at full framework color.
implementation:
- Dashes: build instanceDistanceStart/End yourself, per arc, instead of calling computeLineDistances. For each arc of length L and period P, set n = max(2, round(L/P)) and scale = nP/L, so distance restarts at 0 and every arc begins and ends on a dash at its pillar. Write the values into the InstancedInterleavedBuffer that computeLineDistances would have produced (copy its layout from three's LineSegments2 source). Delete the marching code: the animated flag, dashOffset and the useFrame block.
- Bundling: in arcsFor, group bundles by `${pa.framework}|${pb.framework}`, compute the hubs once per pair, then sample CubicBezierCurve3(a, c1, c2, z).getPoints(40). Add washOf(count) and pass a per-arc wash into batch() instead of the fixed 0.35.
- Focus: keep the pillar instances in the order of layout.positions keys, plus an id→index map. When focus changes, run setColorAt over all instances, set instanceColor.needsUpdate, and call invalidate(). For picking, map e.instanceId to an id. Keep the selection/hover rims as separate meshes (at most two) or a two-instance hexRimGeometry.
- Use frameloop="demand". Call invalidate after focus or size changes and after the fog density write in Rig.
- Acceptance checks:
  - Unit test: all four LINK_DASH entries are distinct.
  - Unit test: arc distances start at 0 for every arc.
  - Unit test: snapshot of nexusLayout positions is unchanged.
  - Unit test: arc endpoints are unchanged.
  - Draw calls at rest ≤ 15 (renderer.info).
  - renderer.info.render.frame stays the same over 2s of idle.
  - Existing e2e visual baselines are refreshed and reviewed by a person.
  - Keyboard selection from the 2D list still frames the camera.
risks: Hover on InstancedMesh: R3F keys hover by object plus instanceId, so moving between pillars should fire out/over. Check that the cursor and onHover(null) don't flicker or get stuck.

Demand rendering: confirm drei CameraControls calls invalidate during smoothTime transitions. If it doesn't, add an 'update' listener that calls invalidate. If transitions stall, demand mode is the cause.
Manually written line distances depend on three's internal attribute layout. Pin the three version or add a test that fails if the attribute names change.
With β too high, trunks hide which group an arc belongs to. Keep β ≤ 0.6 and check that the focused arcs still end at the right pillars.

Ghost arcs at 0.14 opacity may still be too busy with about 960 bundles. Fall back to the old 'hide all' if contrast tests fail, and keep the color of the legend's 'not enabled' pillars distinct from dimmed pillars.
preserveDrawingBuffer: true adds per-frame cost. Leave it on only if the screenshot scripts need it.
World-unit dots shrink as you zoom out. Past about 200 units, dotted and solid lines may look alike. Accept this or limit maxDistance for threat-focused views.
